items.argument_or_counterexample: A numerical simulation and identical response curves do not establish a brain or mechanical system's actual comparator, reference-read or consumer paths. Same stored reference values do not establish same executed use.
items.recommended_action: Ground one actual instance and its independently fixed consumer ports; distinguish source statements, measurements and assumed circuit roles.
items.verification_basis: Manual algebra/countermodels and MODEL_RESULTS.json establish only the model-level claim. Actual implementation and semantic bridge are not discharged.

items.argument_or_counterexample: S/C produce identical report laws for all admitted inputs while q and U differ. Nonreport motor output alone also need not identify experienced temporal content. C1 preserves a grounded structural predicate without naming felt order.
items.recommended_action: Specify one independently motivated relation-to-content bridge and its competing explanation. Accept only source-grounded evidence or a scoped impossibility result; do not close via PASS counts.

items.argument_or_counterexample: Pairwise time coordination can fail to admit one additive coordinate; coordinate existence conversely selects no unique subject. Content change does not imply richer total experience.
items.recommended_action: Keep subject individuation, additive compatibility, ordinal consistency and richness distinct in the retained giant-network and split-brain experiments.

items.argument_or_counterexample: A second output separates only the specified fixed architectures; a hidden beta path, changed readout calibration or nonisolated intervention can mimic the contrast.
items.recommended_action: Compare one concrete rival with independently constrained paths. State which assumption fails if the contrast is absent; do not claim identification of all possible mechanisms.
